transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello. Well, I came in because my sleep has really fallen apart lately. I’m usually a very disciplined sleeper, but... since my cousin died, I just lie awake replaying that night. 

And then when I do finally drop off, I end up waking at 3 or 4 in the morning from these scraps of hospital images in my head. It's becoming a real problem for my work. I have to go into board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces, and I just can't keep functioning like this.
How long ago did your cousin die?
It was about three weeks ago. That's when the... well, that's when the highway collision happened. So, yeah, this has all been going on since that night.
Since the collision, have you been deliberately avoiding reminders of what happened?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I haven't been going out of my way to avoid anything, if that's what you mean. I still drive my usual routes, I haven't put away photos or anything like that. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm deliberately avoiding reminders. It's really just the nights and the lack of sleep that are the problem.
Since the collision, have you been unusually jumpy or easily startled?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm not jumping at shadows or sudden noises, if that's what you're asking. I feel pretty normal during the day, aside from just being exhausted. It's really just the sleep issues that are bothering me.
Apart from your sleep problems, have you been feeling anxious or on edge during the day since the collision?

Well, I suppose I do feel it when I'm driving. I've noticed I keep checking my mirrors constantly, and I'm always watching the speed of the trucks around me, trying to figure out where I could pull off if I needed to. Even just on the familiar roads I take to the office, my body stays really tight... it's like I'm just waiting for something to happen. So, yes, I guess I am pretty on edge whenever I'm in the car.
Were you personally present at the highway collision, or did you learn about your cousin’s death afterward?

I... I think there might be some confusion. I was personally in the collision, yes. I was the one driving. But I'm not sure what you mean about my cousin. None of my family members were involved in this, and no one passed away. It was just me out there on the highway.
What do you remember about the collision itself?

I remember the moments right before the impact, but... well, what frightens me is what I don't remember right after. I can account for all the practical arrangements I made later that day, like the insurance calls and contacting my office to clear my schedule. But parts of the police call at the scene, and what exactly happened when I first reached the hospital... they are simply blank. 

I'm used to being sharp and keeping track of every detail for my business, so having these missing pieces in my memory is just not like me at all.
Are the memory gaps limited to the collision and the time immediately afterward, or do they also affect memories from other parts of your life?

No, it's really just limited to that specific window of time. Everything else is perfectly fine. I remember my schedule, conversations I've had, things from before the accident... everything else in my life is as clear as it usually is. It's just that brief period right around the crash and at the hospital that I can't seem to piece together.
Since the collision, have you felt detached from yourself, as though you were observing yourself from outside your body?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I mean, I feel very much... present in my own body. I haven't had any sort of out-of-body experience or felt disconnected from who I am. It's really just those missing pieces of time that are bothering me.
Did you sustain a head injury during the collision?

No, I didn't. I didn't hit my head on the steering wheel or anything like that. The doctors at the hospital checked me over and... well, they didn't find any signs of a concussion or head trauma. Physically, my head is completely fine.
When you try hard to remember what happened during that missing period, does it remain completely inaccessible despite your being awake and medically alert at the time?

Yes, it really is. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't retrieve it. What frightens me is that I can clearly account for the funeral arrangements and the calls I made afterward, but parts of the police call and what exactly happened when I reached the hospital are simply blank. I know I was awake and alert, but those specific moments are just gone... which is not like me at all.
